invariants: The full distil workflow behaves exactly as it does today for every existing source kind: no switch makes it extract, verify or reconcile less deeply.
Every backlog written before this change still passes the backlog check, and the build loop reads it as it does today.
No new command wraps the GitHub CLI or the GitHub API: pull requests, checks and merges stay plain gh calls in the skill's steps.

increments.detail: Today a ticket reaches the full distil only as a plain document, as the save and continue programme had to do, so its acceptance criteria, comments and attachments lose their structure. A ticket becomes a source kind of its own, with an extract method that reads the description, every acceptance criterion as its own claim, comments as context and each attachment in turn. This is also what lets ticket mode hand a ticket that turns out too big over to the full distil without losing anything.

increments.title: One command fetches a ticket into a new ticket workarea, with its branch named
increments.detail: Ticket mode starts from a Jira key and nothing else. increments.title: The backlog check holds a ticket backlog to its ticket's acceptance criteria
increments.detail: A ticket backlog has no requirements file, so the distil coverage check cannot say whether every acceptance criterion is built. The backlog envelope gains the ticket key it builds, and may carry its branch as a split backlog does. A new intake record lists every statement of the ticket and the rows that cover it, or why it is not built. The backlog check then refuses a ticket backlog that leaves a criterion uncovered and unexplained, covers one with a row that does not exist or is set aside, cites a statement the record does not have, or carries themes or split-off pointers.
acceptanceCriteria: A backlog whose envelope names a ticket and a branch passes the backlog check when every acceptance criterion in its intake record is covered by a todo, blocked or done row, or has a reason it is not built (document:ticket-to-backlog-plan §2 Ticket backlogs in the one shape)
The check refuses a ticket backlog with an acceptance criterion neither covered nor explained, and names the criterion in plain words (document:ticket-to-backlog-plan §2)
The check refuses a criterion covered only by a dropped, rejected or merged-into row, or by a row id the backlog does not have (document:ticket-to-backlog-plan §2)

The check refuses themes, split-off pointers and moved-out pointers on a ticket backlog (document:ticket-to-backlog-plan §2)
Every existing backlog in workareas/shared passes or fails the check exactly as it did before (document:ticket-to-backlog-plan invariants)

increments.title: One command cuts a ticket's branch in every repo it builds and in the workspace, ready for draft pull requests
increments.detail: The branch lifecycle refuses to start until the branch exists with an open pull request in every repo, the workspace included, because the loop syncs main into the workspace and commits the behaviour spec there. Today the session makes these by hand, with an empty opening commit so GitHub will open a pull request. The existing branch command gains an open mode: it takes the branch from the backlog envelope, includes the workspace, adds one empty opening commit where the branch has none of its own, and reports which repos still need a push and a pull request. It never pushes and never calls GitHub, so the pre-push quality gate runs on the session's own push and pull requests stay plain gh calls.

increments.title: The intake workflow turns a fetched ticket into a refuted backlog, a readiness verdict and its questions
increments.detail: Between the fetched ticket and the build, one Opus agent reads the ticket in full and the code it touches, writes an investigation, the intake record and the rows in the one backlog shape, and gives the ticket a readiness verdict by the refinement check's own rules. A different Opus agent then tries to refute every row and statement, finds what was missed and challenges every question. The first agent fixes once from those verdicts. The backlog check runs after each write. The run returns the rows, the verdict, the questions with their defaults, any reason to escalate to the full distil, and the calls the reader made.
